MADtv is an American late-night sketch comedy television series that originally aired on the Fox network from October 14, 1995, to May 16, 2009, spanning 14 seasons. Initially created by Fax Bahr and Adam Small and loosely inspired by the satirical style of Mad magazine, the show was developed to compete directly against NBC’s Saturday Night Live (SNL) by targeting a younger, more diverse audience. Unlike SNL, MADtv mostly bypassed celebrity hosts, was pre-recorded, and focused heavily on aggressive pop-culture parodies, crude humor, and recurring original characters like Stuart Larkin and Ms. Swan. The show launched or advanced the careers of notable comedic talents such as Alex Borstein, Keegan-Michael Key, Jordan Peele, and Michael McDonald. Budget constraints and rising production costs ultimately led to its cancellation by Fox in 2009, though it remains remembered as SNL’s longest-running rival and briefly returned for an eight-episode revival on The CW in 2016.
